label: Clay
title: Clay of the soil, by parish
subtitle: USDA soil survey (SSURGO), average of the top 30 cm
source: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Geographic Database (SSURGO)
how: Each parish is coloured by its average clay (particles under 0.002 mm) as a percent of the soil, from the official USDA soil survey, for the top 30 cm of soil. Each map unit is weighted by its area.
limits: Values are averages of the top 30 cm, over every soil map unit in the parish weighted by its area. One parish holds many different soils, so a field can differ a lot from the parish average.
The soil survey describes soils from field surveys and lab samples. The numbers are the survey's representative values, not measurements of a particular field.
Some soil survey areas cover two parishes or part of a parish; those values are shared between the parishes they cover.
Soil changes slowly, but liming, fertiliser, drainage and flooding change pH, organic matter and salinity locally. Soil tests are the reliable guide for a field.

credits.text: Soils: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service, Soil Survey Geographic Database (SSURGO), through Soil Data Access
Parish boundaries: US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain)
